paras: The short-tailed striped gecko (Strophurus mcmillani), also known commonly as McMillan's spiny-tailed gecko, is a species of lizard in the family Diplodactylidae. The species is endemic to Australia.
The specific name, mcmillani, is in honor of Australian entomologist Robert Peter McMillan (1921–2009).
In Australia, Strophurus mcmillani is found in extreme northwestern Northern Territory and in Western Australia.
The natural habitats of Strophurus mcmillani are grassland and rocky areas.

Strophurus mcmillani has an average snout-to-vent length (SVL) of 4.5 cm (1.8 in), and the average tail length is 61% of the SVL. Dorsally and laterally, it is olive grey, with dark brown and white stripes.
